# Independent audit: exposed source-fiber rays and convex hinge efficiency

Source: `candidate 2d5d7d5b889b668f`.

Full proof audit: PASS. No correction required.

The nonzero continuous normal condition and the generic ray choice make
every cap margin at both ray endpoints strictly nonzero. The two profile
values therefore sum exactly to one, with no closed-boundary replacement.
Both endpoints are actual points of the same source fiber. If the chosen
point is exposed in the ambient C, compactness supplies a genuine positive
exposing-functional gap outside a sign-constant neighborhood. The hinge
is convex on the full physical space, vanishes outside that neighborhood
on the actual boundary measure, and has finite positive integral. In
particular it does not purport to concentrate a convex function at an
arbitrary interior point of an exposed facet.

The positive-integral step is valid for an arbitrary full-dimensional
convex source fiber: radial projection from its interior point sends a
small open spherical patch into the positive-hinge boundary neighborhood;
standard local convex boundary charts, or the locally Lipschitz radial
map and its inverse, give positive (d-1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure.
For d=1 the endpoint carries positive counting mass. Compact convex
full-dimensional fibers have finite surface area, and only finitely many
fibers are used.

In the strictly convex ambient case, a fiber-boundary point cannot be
interior to C. Every supporting face of C is a singleton, so every such
point is exposed. The corollary consequently follows without a general
position assumption or an unjustified density-of-exposed-points argument.
It needs neither criticality nor circuit balance, but does retain source
interiority and nonvertical caps.

The final scope limitation is essential and correctly stated: there is
no upper semicontinuity conclusion for the optimized potential cone at a
nonstrictly-convex limit. The exact R4 perturbation provides an independent
actual calibration of precisely that discontinuity. This lemma alone does
not resolve the regularity or selected-circuit interface at an arbitrary
attained shape minimum, and it does not prove OC.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
